# enco:plugin@0.9.0

Enco plugin contract. Plugins interact with the host only through these imports.

## Worlds

### `base`

Imports and lifecycle operations shared by all plugins.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: lifecycle

### `provider-plugin`

A plugin exposing completion and embedding operations.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: completion, embedding, lifecycle

### `completion-plugin`

A plugin exposing model completion.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: completion, lifecycle

### `embedding-plugin`

A plugin exposing text embedding.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: embedding, lifecycle

### `decision-plugin`

A plugin exposing typed decisions over shared evidence.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: decision, lifecycle

### `tool-plugin`

A plugin exposing model-facing tools.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: tools, lifecycle

### `composer-plugin`

A plugin that writes model requests.

- Imports: types, host
- Exports: composer, lifecycle

### `channel-plugin`

A messaging protocol's mapper. It imports nothing; the host trusts it with the connection's
account.

- Imports: types
- Exports: lifecycle, channel

#### enum `effect`

Mutation semantics used to order calls and settle interrupted work.

Consecutive read-only calls run together; other calls run one at a time. A call cut off by
a crash fails as retryable when it is read-only, and settles as unknown otherwise.

- `read-only`: Changes nothing beyond its result.
- `idempotent`: Making the call again has the same effect as making it once.
- `side-effect`: Changes something that must not be changed again blindly.

#### record `tool-spec`

A tool disclosed to the model.

`input-schema` describes the argument object in a subset of JSON Schema:
- objects with `properties` and `required`, always with `additionalProperties: false`;
- strings with `enum`, `minLength` and `maxLength`;
- integers and numbers with `minimum` and `maximum`;
- booleans;
- arrays with `items`, `minItems` and `maxItems`;
- `anyOf` with two or more schemas.

Any schema below the root may carry a `description` and a `default` that fits it; the root
is an object and carries neither. A declaration outside the subset fails to load. The host
checks every call against the schema before the plugin sees it: an optional property given
as null counts as not given, and an integer written with a zero fraction, such as 5.0,
arrives as 5.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The name the model calls the tool by: ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, unique among the plugin's tools. |
| `description` | `string` | What the tool does, for the model to read. |
| `input-schema` | `json` | The argument object, in the subset of JSON Schema stated above. |
| `effect` | `effect` | What a call may change; completion adapters ignore it, and the host uses it when dispatching. |

#### variant `outcome`

A known result, a known failure, or an external effect that cannot be confirmed.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ok` | `json` | The call succeeded with this JSON result. |
| `failed` | `failure` | The call failed, and its effects are known. |
| `unknown` | `failure` | An external effect may have happened and cannot be confirmed; it is never retried automatically. |

#### variant `unviewable-reason`

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|

| `too-large` | `_` | It is larger than an image may be. |
| `unavailable` | `string` | It could not be retrieved, for this reason. |

#### record `unviewable`

An attachment kept only as a description.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `what` | `string` | The channel's description of it. |
| `reason` | `unviewable-reason` | Why it is not an image. |

#### func `config`

```wit
config: func() -> json;
```

The configuration of this invocation's generation, excluding credential mappings.

#### func `log`

```wit
log: func(level: log-level, message: string);
```

Write a diagnostic to the host log.

#### func `http`

```wit
http: async func(request: http-request) -> result<http-response, http-failure>;
```

Send a request and collect its response; non-2xx statuses are returned as responses.

The host attaches declared credentials only to the bound origin (scheme, host and port),
overriding the matching request header. Redirects are followed only within that origin.
Cross-origin redirects are returned unchanged. Credential values in response headers,
bodies and failures are replaced with [redacted:<environment variable name>].
Encoded forms of a credential (such as base64) are not redacted.

### `tools`

Model-facing tools whose definitions are fixed with their generation.

#### func `list`

```wit
list: func(config: json) -> list<tool-spec>;
```

Project tool definitions from configuration already accepted by `lifecycle.describe`.

Definitions are fixed with the generation, so this runs without network access.

#### func `call`

```wit
call: async func(name: string, input: json) -> outcome;
```

Execute one tool.

`input` already fits the tool's `input-schema`; validate only what the schema cannot
express. Return an unknown outcome when an external effect may have occurred but is
unconfirmed.

# Errors
Failure codes are `provider.network`, `provider.auth`, `provider.rate_limited`,
`provider.server`, `provider.bad_request`, `provider.bad_response`, and `timeout`.

### `embedding`

Embeds texts for retrieval independently of model completion.

#### func `embed`

```wit
embed: async func(settings: settings, inputs: list<string>) -> result<list<list<f32>>, failure>;
```

Return exactly one nonempty vector of finite numbers per input, in input order.
All returned vectors must have the same width.

# Errors
Uses `provider.*` failure codes and `timeout`, as in `completion.complete`.

# Errors
Uses `provider.*` failure codes and `timeout`, as in `completion.complete`.

### `composer`

Writes the model requests of the Sessions whose profile names this plugin.

A composition is a pure function of its arguments, the plugin's configuration and its own code,
and changes nothing but its result: it has no files, no environment variables and no network, so
`host.http` fails. The wall clock reads the Round's instant, the monotonic clock stands still and
randomness is seeded by the Round, so the same generation, called again within a Round with the
same arguments, returns the same plan.

The host records each plan before sending it and resolves its Log references. A plan breaks
this contract when it discloses a capability outside this Round, refers to a position outside
the transcript, or sends images to a model that does not accept them; when a reply plan leaves
out a capability in `lifeline`; or when a compaction discloses any tool or stops where no Round
ends.

|---|---|---|
| `budget` | `budget` | Its limits. |
| `accepts` | `list<modality>` | What it accepts besides text. |
| `skipped` | `list<skipped-endpoint>` | Earlier candidates that are unavailable or exhausted in this Run, in configured order. |

#### record `source`

A source a plan renders, with a digest a later composition can compare.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `string` | The source, such as `memory:<id>`. |
| `hash` | `string` | The BLAKE3 digest of its text before formatting, in lowercase hex. |

#### record `inline`

Text the composer wrote, recorded verbatim.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | `role` | Who speaks. |
| `text` | `string` | The exact words the host will record and send to the model. |
| `sources` | `list<source>` | The sources it renders, in order. |

#### record `log-ref`

A Log message the request repeats.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `pos` | `log-pos` | The message, by its position in the transcript. |
| `images` | `bool` | Whether its images go with it; all of them or none. |

#### variant `plan-item`

One message of a request.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | `inline` | Text the composer wrote. |
| `log` | `log-ref` | A message from the Log. |

#### record `plan`

A request, before the host records and resolves it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `list<plan-item>` | The messages, in order. |
| `tools` | `list<capability-id>` | The tools to disclose, by identity. |
| `max-output-tokens` | `option<u32>` | The most tokens the reply may use; the service's default when absent. |
| `omitted` | `list<omission>` | What the composer left out, and why. |

#### record `compose-input`

Everything the host supplies for one composition.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `session` | `session` | The Session the request is for. |
| `timezone` | `string` | The owner's time zone, as an IANA name such as `Asia/Shanghai`. |
| `home` | `string` | The home's absolute path on the node running this Round.  Its layout is part of this contract: `config.toml`, `AGENTS.md` for the standing instructions, `plugins/<name>/`, `sdk/`, `manual/` and `workspace/`. `.data/` is Enco's own store and not part of it. |
| `transcript` | `transcript` | The conversation as it stands, which a plan may refer to.  After a backtrack it is the Log up to the backtrack's target, then everything from the backtrack on, so positions can skip. |
| `previous` | `option<plan>` | The latest recorded reply plan in that conversation; absent at the start, or when it could not be read, which `omitted` then says. |
| `instructions` | `option<string>` | The text of `AGENTS.md`, as read at the start of this Round; absent when the file does not exist, and in safe mode. |
| `memories` | `list<memory>` | Memories for this Round in priority order: pinned ones first, then those recalled for the latest input, most relevant first; empty in safe mode. |
| `omitted` | `list<omission>` | Content the host could not supply; the host records it with the plan. |
| `capabilities` | `list<capability>` | Every tool this Round may disclose; in safe mode, only the lifeline. |
| `lifeline` | `list<capability-id>` | The tools every reply plan must disclose; empty when the Session does not require the lifeline. |
| `unavailable` | `list<unavailable-plugin>` | Plugins left out of this Round. |
| `safe-mode` | `option<safe-mode>` | Why this Round runs in safe mode; absent in normal operation. |
| `reply` | `reply-target` | The model a reply plan is for. |
| `compaction` | `option<budget>` | The summarizing model's limits; absent when no summarizing model is usable. |
| `compactions-left` | `u32` | How many more compactions this Round allows. |

#### record `compaction`

A request to summarize history before replying.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `upto` | `log-pos` | The last Round end to summarize, one of `transcript.round-ends`. |
| `plan` | `plan` | The summarizing request; it discloses no tools. |

#### variant `composition`

What a composition returns.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `reply` | `plan` | A reply request. |
| `compact` | `compaction` | Summarize history first; the host composes again once the summary is recorded. |

#### func `options-schema`

```wit
options-schema: func(config: json) -> json;
```

The JSON Schema of the options a profile passes to `compose`, in the subset `tool-spec`
states.

An empty object must fit it. The host checks a profile's options against the schema of the
generation that runs them: registering configuration or code that breaks a profile's options
is rejected, and a profile whose options no longer fit, as after a rollback, cannot use this
plugin until they do. The schema is fixed with the generation, so this runs without network
access.

#### func `compose`

```wit
compose: func(options: json, input: compose-input) -> result<composition, failure>;
```

Write the next request.

`options` fit the running generation's `options-schema` and are normalized as tool arguments
are. Return `compact` only while `compaction` is present and `compactions-left` is above
zero.

# Errors
`context.overflow` when no valid request fits the window; when only a compaction would make
it fit and `compaction` is absent, the host records why no summarizing model is usable. The
host records any other code as `compose.failed`.

### `channel`

Translates a messaging protocol as a pure state machine; the host owns connections, timers and credentials.

The host records each external input before handing it over, and carries out what the mapper asks.

#### record `request`

A request for the host to send.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` | The method, such as `GET` or `POST`. |
| `url` | `string` | A path starting with `/`, joined to the connection's base URL, or an absolute URL at one of the mapper's `origins`. |
| `headers` | `list<tuple<string, string>>` | Header names and values, in order. |
| `body` | `option<list<u8>>` | The bytes to send, if any. |
| `timeout-ms` | `option<u32>` | The time limit in milliseconds; the host's default when absent. |

#### record `response`

A response the protocol returned, whatever its status.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `u16` | The status code, such as 200. |
| `headers` | `list<tuple<string, string>>` | Header names and values, in order. |
| `body` | `list<u8>` | The whole body. |

#### record `socket`

A WebSocket the host opens and keeps until the mapper asks to reconnect or the connection
stops.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | `string` | An absolute `ws` or `wss` URL at one of the mapper's `origins`. |
| `close-code` | `u16` | The code the host closes the socket with; a protocol that resumes sessions across reconnects may need one other than 1000. |

#### variant `read-step`

How the host reads the protocol next.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `request` | Send this request; its response is one arrival. |
| `socket` | `socket` | Open this socket; each frame on it is one arrival, until it closes. |

#### record `closure`

How a socket ended.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | `option<u16>` | The close code, when the protocol sent one. |
| `reason` | `string` | The close reason, or the host's description of the network failure. |

#### variant `arrival`

Something that reached the mapper through the host.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `response` | `response` | The response to the read request. |
| `frame` | `string` | A text frame on the open socket. |
| `closed` | `closure` | The socket closed, by the protocol or through a network failure. |
| `timer` | `_` | The timer the mapper set has expired; its reading can change state and request actions, but has no inbound messages. |

#### record `fault`

What a protocol answer means for the host's settlement and retries.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `failure` | `failure` | What failed. |
| `unknown` | `bool` | The request may have taken effect, so it must not be sent again. |
| `fatal` | `bool` | The whole connection is unusable, not just this request or destination. |
| `retry-after` | `option<u32>` | How long the protocol asks to wait before retrying, in seconds. |

#### record `identity`

The account a connection reaches.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | `string` | A nonempty protocol name without colons; with `account`, it keys connection state. |
| `account` | `string` | A nonempty, stable account ID within the protocol, treated as opaque by the host. |
| `facts` | `json` | What the mapper needs to know about the account later, such as the bot's username. |

#### record `attachment`

An image attachment described by its protocol locator.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `what` | `string` | What the attachment is, for a message that cannot show it. |
| `locator` | `string` | The opaque locator passed to `fetch`. |

#### record `content`

The text and attachments of a message.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | What the sender wrote. |
| `images` | `list<attachment>` | Images, by the protocol's locator for fetching them. |
| `unviewable` | `list<unviewable>` | Attachments that cannot be images, and why. |

#### variant `action`

What an incoming message asks for, whatever the protocol's command syntax.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | `content` | A message for the conversation's Session. |
| `sessions` | `_` | List the Sessions to choose from. |
| `select-session` | `string` | Route this conversation to the named Session. |
| `cancel` | `_` | Stop the work the conversation's Session is doing. |
| `backtrack` | `_` | Take the conversation back to the message `reply-to` names. |
| `everyone` | `option<bool>` | Open this group to everyone or close it to the owner only; absent reports which. |

#### record `inbound`

A message that arrived, as the protocol describes it.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `string` | The protocol's key for accepting this message once, such as an update or event ID. |
| `conversation` | `string` | The conversation, where replies go. |
| `message` | `string` | This message's ID, unique within the conversation. |
| `sender` | `option<string>` | The sender's ID, when the protocol reports one. |
| `sender-name` | `option<string>` | The sender's display name, when the protocol reports one. |
| `direct` | `bool` | Whether the conversation is one to one. |
| `addressed` | `bool` | Whether the message is addressed to this bot; always true in a direct conversation. |
| `reply-to` | `option<string>` | The message this one replies to, or the message a command was invoked on. |
| `respond` | `option<string>` | The handle for answering this message once accepted, when the protocol expects an answer, such as for a command or a button. |
| `action` | `action` | What it asks for. |

#### record `reading`

What the mapper asks of the host after one arrival.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `messages` | `list<inbound>` | Messages to accept, in order. |
| `state` | `option<json>` | The protocol state after this arrival; absent leaves it unchanged.  The host uses it for the next call at once, and commits it once every message of this reading is accepted. |
| `frames` | `list<string>` | Text frames to send on the socket now, in order. |
| `acknowledgments` | `list<request>` | Protocol acknowledgments to send before acceptance, with no effect beyond confirming receipt.  Answers to this reading's messages are sent only after these complete. |
| `timer` | `option<u32>` | Milliseconds until a `timer` arrival, replacing any pending timer; absent keeps it. Timers end with the socket. |
| `reconnect` | `bool` | Close the socket and start the next read with `read`. |

#### record `file-data`

File bytes for one outgoing message.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The filename without its original directory. |
| `data` | `list<u8>` | The original bytes, encoded by the mapper for transport. |

#### record `outgoing`

Markdown text with at most one file to send.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | All text to send, in Markdown. |
| `file` | `option<file-data>` | A file to send with this text, if any. |

#### enum `command-kind`

The commands the host understands.

- `session`: List the Sessions, or switch to the one named after it.
- `cancel`: Stop the work of the conversation's Session.
- `backtrack`: Go back to the message the command replies to.
- `everyone`: Open the group to everyone, or close it to the owner only.

#### record `command`

A command the host understands, as it should appear in the protocol's menus.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `command-kind` | Which command. |
| `description` | `string` | What it does, for the menu. |
| `direct` | `bool` | Whether it applies in one-to-one conversations. |
| `group` | `bool` | Whether it applies in group conversations. |

#### variant `fetch-step`

The next step of fetching an attachment.

| Case | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `request` | `request` | Send this request and call again with its response. |
| `image` | `list<u8>` | The attachment's bytes. |
| `unavailable` | `string` | The protocol refused it for good; the text says why. |

#### enum `tool-state`

Where a tool call stands.

- `running`: The call has started and has no settlement yet.
- `ok`: It succeeded.
- `failed`: The call finished with a known failure.
- `unknown`: It may have taken effect, but its result is not known.

#### record `tool-activity`

One tool call shown in an activity view.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The tool's name, as the model calls it. |
| `state` | `tool-state` | Where the call stands. |

#### record `activity-view`

What the Agent is doing while a Run goes on.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `elapsed-seconds` | `u32` | Seconds since the Run started. |
| `tools` | `list<tool-activity>` | The Run's latest tool calls, oldest first. |

#### func `origins`

```wit
origins: func() -> list<string>;
```

Additional origins for requests and sockets; `*.` before a host covers its subdomains. Read when the generation loads.

#### func `identify`

```wit
identify: func() -> request;
```

The request that reads which account the connection reaches.

#### func `identified`

```wit
identified: func(response: response) -> result<identity, fault>;
```

The account in that request's response.

#### func `read`

```wit
read: func(identity: identity, state: option<json>) -> result<read-step, fault>;
```

How to read next, from the latest protocol state; `state` is absent before the protocol
gave one.

`channel.invalid_state` means the state cannot be resumed. The host clears only that
state and retries from `none`, keeping routes and other committed business facts. If the
mapper rejects `none` too, the host stops the connection.

#### func `received`

```wit
received: func(identity: identity, state: option<json>, arrival: arrival) -> result<reading, fault>;
```

What an arrival means, given the latest protocol state.

#### func `fetch`

```wit
fetch: func(locator: string, responses: list<response>) -> result<fetch-step, fault>;
```

The next step of fetching the attachment at `locator`, given the responses so far.

#### func `split`

```wit
split: func(message: outgoing) -> list<outgoing>;
```

The parts an outgoing message is sent as, keeping all of its text.

#### func `send`

```wit
send: func(conversation: string, part: outgoing) -> result<request, fault>;
```

The request that sends one part to a conversation.

#### func `answered`

```wit
answered: func(response: response) -> result<option<string>, fault>;
```

What the protocol answered: the ID of the message a request created, if any, or why it
failed.

#### func `respond`

```wit
respond: func(handle: string, text: option<string>) -> result<option<request>, fault>;
```

The request that answers the accepted message carrying `handle`, showing `text` to its
sender; absent when nothing more needs sending.

#### func `commands`

```wit
commands: func(identity: identity, commands: list<command>) -> list<request>;
```

Requests that offer the host's commands in the protocol's menus, sent when a connection
starts.

#### func `activity`

```wit
activity: func(conversation: string, shown: option<string>, activity: option<activity-view>) -> option<request>;
```

Creates or refreshes the activity view, or removes `shown` when `activity` is absent; absent when nothing needs sending.

The host reads the response to a request made without `shown` with `answered`, and keeps
the message ID it gives as `shown`. Without an ID, it asks again at each refresh.
